articles.title: NFL radio host confesses she would have a baby with Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza
articles.standfirst: Mendoza’s meteoric rise has Raiders fans dreaming big
articles.summary: Mendoza’s meteoric rise has Raiders fans dreaming big
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza's arrival in Las Vegas has already generated enormous excitement, but one NFL radio personality took that enthusiasm to an entirely different level.

Damon Bruce made a wild admission while discussing the Raiders rookie on The What Wright Show, saying he was “personally ready” to have Mendoza's baby if the quarterback asked.

“I am personally ready to have Fernando Mendoza’s baby if he asked me to have it. Like, I love the guy. They should expect nothing short of miracles,” said Bruce .

“He’s already done the football equivalent of walking on water. Heisman, undefeated national title. And if you can win at Indiana, you might even be able to be the guy who can turn the Raiders around. He’s almost too good to be true, boy-scouty.”

The tongue-in-cheek remark highlighted just how quickly the No. 1 overall pick has captured the imagination of Raiders supporters.

Mendoza has arrived in the NFL carrying an extraordinary résumé. After beginning his college career at California, he transferred to Indiana and became the centerpiece of one of college football's most dramatic turnarounds.

He helped transform the Hoosiers into a national powerhouse, ultimately winning the Heisman Trophy and leading Indiana to a national championship before becoming the first overall pick in the NFL draft.

However, the Raiders aren't rushing their young quarterback into the starting role. Veteran Kirk Cousins has been named the team's starter, leaving Mendoza to concentrate on learning the offense and adapting to the speed and physicality of professional football.

His preseason debut nevertheless gave fans plenty to be excited about. Against the Arizona Cardinals, Mendoza completed 10 of 16 passes for 97 yards and a touchdown.

He also contributed six rushing yards while taking one sack. The rookie showed composure during several promising drives, offering an early glimpse of why Las Vegas invested the top pick in him.

Mendoza's latest opportunity raises the excitement

Mendoza's development took another significant step during Tuesday's joint practice with the Houston Texans. For the first time during training camp, the rookie received extensive first-team repetitions, allowing him to go up against Houston's starters and experience a more demanding level of competition.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak explained that putting Mendoza against the Texans' first unit had been part of the team's plan. The practice wasn't perfect, with Houston's defense creating pressure and forcing turnovers, but the young quarterback still produced some encouraging moments.

One of the highlights came when Mendoza escaped pressure before finding tight end Brock Bowers for a substantial gain. Facing a defense that ranked first in the NFL in yards allowed last season provided a valuable test for the rookie.

Mendoza also received a strong endorsement from Texans defensive star Will Anderson Jr. after the practice.

"Ton of respect for him…He's going to be a really great quarterback in this league," Anderson said.

That type of recognition is significant for a rookie who's still adjusting to the professional game. Mendoza has repeatedly acknowledged that the NFL represents a major jump from college football, and the Raiders appear determined to give him the time and experience needed to handle that transition.

Cousins remains the starter for now, but Mendoza's trajectory is already generating plenty of optimism around Las Vegas. Every first-team rep and impressive preseason play gives fans another reason to believe the rookie could eventually become the franchise quarterback they've been waiting for.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza takes Jameis Winston's throne among NFL media: "He is one of those rare birds"
articles.standfirst: Mendoza is already a favorite in media circles even though he's only a rookie.
articles.summary: Mendoza is already a favorite in media circles even though he's only a rookie.
articles.body:
Whether he had nerves or not, Fernando Mendoza can say that he got them out of the way last week. Making his Las Vegas Raiders debut, Mendoza played relatively well, avoiding turnovers while completing 10-of-16 passes for 97 yards and a touchdown .

Now, the fun part starts. Kirk Cousins is still the team's starting quarterback until further notice, but Mendoza will be waiting in the wings and be ready once his number is called . For now, though, Mendoza is saying all of the right things .

That's par for the course for him, given that Mendoza became somewhat of a national darling among football fans during his 2025 season with Indiana due to his genuine personality . It's not only fans who he's won over either; the national media absolutely loves him .

Fernando Mendoza is beloved and will be for a while by the national media

ESPN's Peter Schrager recently delved into why Mendoza is so liked among the media, and he likened him to fellow quarterback Jameis Winston .

Every so often, there's a player in the NFL who comes across and just gives you gold when they get him on the mic. Jameis Winston for years was that guy. I think we have a new king, though... I love this kid. He's authentic. He loves football. He's a winner... But there's also this like young, wild spirit to him that he is just himself. I think that we're going to be very happy with soundbites from Mendoza over the course of his career.

Schrager references a recent soundbite from Mendoza in which the rookie describes the "ecosystem" he and his Raiders teammates are trying to build and evolve during practices.

Mendoza is doing and saying all of the right things ahead of his rookie season. Football just comes natural to him.

articles.standfirst: The Raiders visit the Texans with their sights set on a victory in their preparation for the 2026 - 2027 season
articles.summary: The Raiders visit the Texans with their sights set on a victory in their preparation for the 2026 - 2027 season
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL Preseason reaches its third week and now serves up an interconference matchup between the Houston Texans and the Las Vegas Raiders in Houston . It’s the kind of clash that can be deceptive: in August, the score matters less than the minutes handed out by the coaching staffs.

Starters for every game are usually in for one or two series, and from the second half onward the stage belongs to rookies, tryout free agents, and players battling for the last tickets on the 53-man roster; and for this game, it will be no different.

How do the Raiders and Texans enter their preseason matchup?

This is an exhibition matchup between a representative of the AFC South (Texans) and one of the AFC West (Raiders). In the preseason there are no standings implications or playoff pressure: what is at stake is the evaluation of young talent such as that of the new QB Fernando Mendoza , the rhythm of the offense in its first series, and defensive depth.

Houston, at home, will look to give quality minutes to its second unit against a Las Vegas defense that will also be rotating pieces . The directive in both locker rooms will be to come out without injuries and with answers.

Texans - Raiders: Game time and stadium

The opening whistle for the preseason game between Houston and Las Vegas is scheduled for Thursday, August 20, 2026, at 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time . For the rest of the United States, the game will start at:

The setting is NRG Stadium in Houston, Texas, a venue with a capacity of 72,220 spectators and a retractable roof, home of the Texans . It is an ideal environment for August football: controlled climate and a field that allows the passing attack to be seen without weather-related disruptions.

Where can you watch the Texans - Raiders and the rest of the NFL preseason?

For all the audience who enjoys the NFL before the regular season begins, you will be able to follow this game on NFL Network on ESPN ; in addition, you will be able to watch it live via streaming on FUBO.

How is the betting market for Texans - Raiders and for the rest of the NFL Preseason?

The specific lines for this matchup are still not open on the market, which is normal when the game is still several days away . Even so, there are principles you should be clear on before the numbers are released.

"Favoritism carries little weight. In the regular season, the name on the marquee defines the line; in the preseason, it does not. A team can be a contender in September and still lose in August because it sat its starters in the second quarter.

The books adjust the moneyline (straight-up winner, no draw in this sport) more based on roster depth and the coaching staff's intentions than on star talent. Here, Houston's home-field advantage at NRG Stadium is a lesser factor compared with whoever decides to give more reps to their offense.

The total (Over/Under) is the key market to take seriously. Points in the preseason are volatile : they depend on how often the units rotate, the number of turnovers among players trying out, and whether the kickers make their field goals.

When the lines open, it is worth comparing the total number to the historical pace of these games, where low scores are frequent in the first half and scoring spikes when the third-string units come in without defensive adjustments.

The point spread requires context. Remember that in American football the handicap is called the point spread, and in preseason a favorite of -3 or -4 can fall short if it rests its stars too early . The key information is not talent, but the rotation plan: what each coaching staff announced about how many minutes the starters will play.

When the exact money line, total, and point spread odds are posted for this Texans vs. Raiders matchup, the discipline will be the same: compare the number to the minutes plan, prioritize the early Under, and look for value in the depth , not in the stars.

articles.title: Tom Brady has something special planned for Fernando Mendoza as Raiders organization set to undergo major change
articles.standfirst: The Las Vegas Raiders aren't content with what they have right now.
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders aren't content with what they have right now.
articles.body:
Even though the 2025 season went as poorly as possible, the Las Vegas Raiders are actually in a great spot heading into the future. A strong offseason guided by general manager John Spytek , which included securing Fernando Mendoza as their new franchise quarterback, has fans feeling hopeful again.

First-time head coach Klint Kubiak is expected to bring a much fresher perspective to the team than previous coaches, and should help develop and get the best out of Mendoza. All of this is music to Tom Brady 's ears. When Brady purchased a minority stake in the Raiders franchise in 2024, the team was not in a good spot. The 2025 season only set off more alarms. But now, things are changing .

Raiders want to make a $158 million "front door" improvement to Allegiant Stadium

Brady and his ownership partners have their eyes fully set on turning the Raiders into a model NFL franchise. With that in mind, the organization higher-ups are in the process of facilitating a massive $158 million improvement for Allegiant Stadium .

This improvement will essentially turn the stadium's entrance into a large plaza and event space. It all sounds great in theory, but there's one catch: The Raiders want to use $75 million from an existing taxpayer fund for the improvements .

Allegiant Stadium just recently hosted Super Bowl 58 and is scheduled to host Super Bowl 63 . The organization wants to go all-out for that one, with the dream of seeing Mendoza leading the Raiders to The Big Game for that edition.

Of course, the news of these improvements didn't sit well with many fans, given that the stadium just opened in 2020 .

articles.title: What are the Raiders really planning for Fernando Mendoza?
articles.standfirst: The Raiders have a clear plan for Fernando Mendoza — and his next preseason test could reveal what's next.
articles.summary: The Raiders have a clear plan for Fernando Mendoza — and his next preseason test could reveal what's next.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders have made it clear that the development of Fernando Mendoza , the No. 1 overall pick in the NFL Draft , will be a top priority during his rookie season. As part of that plan, the young quarterback is expected to see extended playing time in the first half of Thursday night's preseason matchup against the Houston Texans .

Fernando Mendoza continues to earn the Raiders' trust

During this week's joint practices between the Raiders and Texans, Mendoza worked with the first-team offense, gaining valuable reps against Houston's defense.

Head coach Klint Kubiak said he liked what he saw from the rookie but declined to offer a detailed evaluation.

"...I've got to watch the tape," Kubiak said when asked about Mendoza's performance.

Even so, Kubiak made it clear that Mendoza, along with the rest of the team's young players, still needs to adjust to the speed and intensity of the NFL , a natural part of the rookie learning curve.

Kirk Cousins remains the starter

Barring a surprise, Fernando Mendoza will not open the season as the Raiders' starting quarterback . That role will remain with veteran Kirk Cousins , who enters the year as the leader of the offense.

While Cousins understands that Mendoza is viewed as the franchise's quarterback of the future, the veteran is expected to continue leading the team while also helping mentor and accelerate the rookie's development.

With 44,700 passing yards and 298 touchdown passes over his career , Cousins will look to add to those totals this season while preparing Mendoza to eventually become Las Vegas' franchise quarterback .

articles.title: Tom Brady must be really worried: Fernando Mendoza threw a terrible pick-six with the Raiders
articles.standfirst: Fernando Mendoza’s path to the Raiders’ starting job took a hit.
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza’s path to the Raiders’ starting job took a hit.
articles.body:
F ernando Mendoza ’s first start with the Las Vegas Raiders against the Houston Texans could not have gotten off to a worse start. The rookie quarterback opened the game with most of Las Vegas’ second-team offense around him, but on just his fifth play, he made a mistake that immediately turned into points for the opponent.

Mendoza attempted to complete a short pass over the middle of the field, but linebacker Wade Woodaz read the play perfectly, intercepted the throw and returned it 80 yards for a defensive touchdown .

The play may have been the result of a miscommunication on the Raiders’ offense. Running back Mike Washington appeared to start moving after Mendoza released the ball, leaving Woodaz in the perfect position to make the interception and race untouched to the end zone.

The pick-six came shortly after the Texans’ offense marched down the field on its opening possession and scored a touchdown, quickly giving Houston a 14-0 lead .

The interception was reminiscent of what happened during Tuesday’s joint practices between the Raiders and Texans, when Mendoza also threw a pass that was returned for a touchdown.

In that instance, the mistake came after several strong plays from the rookie. Now, Mendoza will need to show the ability to move past the error and respond as he continues to be evaluated during the preseason.

Mendoza’s mistake could give Cousins more time as Raiders’ starter

Kirk Cousins remains the favorite to open the season as the starting quarterback for the Las Vegas Raiders , a scenario that would allow Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the Draft, to continue developing behind an experienced NFL veteran.

After his impressive performance in the previous game, some began to believe Mendoza could be ready to compete for the starting job immediately. However, his latest outing, highlighted by a pick-six against the Texans, could strengthen the case for keeping Cousins in charge of the offense while the rookie continues his development.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza receives blunt message from Raiders coach Klint Kubiak following 'pick-six' against the Texans
articles.standfirst: First overall pick flashes talent but learns the mistakes young quarterbacks must overcome
articles.summary: First overall pick flashes talent but learns the mistakes young quarterbacks must overcome
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza ’s first preseason start with the Las Vegas Raiders delivered a glimpse of both his potential and the growing pains that come with being a rookie quarterback in the NFL .

After an impressive debut against the Arizona Cardinals raised expectations, Mendoza faced a much tougher challenge against the Houston Texans on Thursday.

The first overall pick showed flashes of confidence and playmaking ability, but a costly interception returned for a touchdown highlighted the areas he still needs to improve.

Mendoza finished the night completing 8 of 15 passes for 86 yards, throwing an 80-yard pick-six that helped Houston build an early lead. Despite the mistake, the Raiders recovered to secure a 22-20 victory, and head coach Klint Kubiak focused more on the lessons than the result.

“I think it’s plenty to clean up, plenty to get better at,” Kubiak said after the game. “Plenty that we can do better for him as coaches, plenty that he can learn from. But with a great heart that we showed in the second half, the whole team, offense, defense, really proud of our guys.”

The biggest mistake came during Mendoza’ s opening drive. After a strong 22-yard completion to Jalen Nailor and a 33-yard run from rookie Mike Washington Jr. moved the Raiders deep into Houston territory, the quarterback attempted to continue the momentum.

Instead, Mendoza forced a throw toward Washington that landed directly in the hands of Texans linebacker Wade Woodaz . The defender returned the interception 80 yards for a touchdown, giving Houston a 14-0 advantage.

It was the type of error that often comes with young quarterbacks adjusting to the speed and complexity of the NFL.

Mendoza finds positives after tough moment

While the turnover grabbed attention, Mendoza showed the ability to respond. The rookie continued to attack downfield, connected with Dylan Laube and Connor Heyward , and helped create a scoring opportunity with a completion to Ian Thomas that led to a Matt Gay field goal.

Mendoza also acknowledged that the Raiders need to become more efficient in key situations, particularly inside the red zone.

“I know it’s tough down there in the red zone, a lot of bodies in a short amount of space, but I feel like we could have done more in the red zone, and I think that is something for us to learn,” Mendoza said.

“It’s one of our focuses this year to be better in the red zone, so we got some work to do.”

The performance came with added importance because veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins , Mendoza ’s main competition for the starting job, didn't play. With an opportunity to strengthen his case, Mendoza instead provided a mixed evaluation.

Kubiak made it clear that the quarterback competition remains open, refusing to guarantee anyone’s place on the depth chart.

“We got another week,” Kubiak said when asked about naming a starter. “I don’t want anyone to be comfortable in their job.”

The Raiders appear willing to let Mendoza develop at his own pace rather than rushing him into action. Cousins provides veteran stability, allowing Las Vegas to give their young quarterback valuable experience without placing the entire burden of the offense on his shoulders.

The pick-six against Houston was a difficult moment, but it was also a necessary part of Mendoza ’s development. The Raiders believe he has the talent to become their long-term answer at quarterback, and learning from mistakes like Thursday’s will be a major part of that journey.

Kubiak made it clear that the quarterback competition remains open, refusing to guarantee anyone’s place on the depth chart.
“We got another week,” Kubiak said when asked about naming a starter. “I don’t want anyone to be comfortable in their job.”

The Raiders appear willing to let Mendoza develop at his own pace rather than rushing him into action. Cousins provides veteran stability, allowing Las Vegas to give their young quarterback valuable experience without placing the entire burden of the offense on his shoulders.

The pick-six against Houston was a difficult moment, but it was also a necessary part of Mendoza ’s development. The Raiders believe he has the talent to become their long-term answer at quarterback, and learning from mistakes like Thursday’s will be a major part of that journey.

articles.title: Gisele Bundchen recalls the date with Tom Brady that changed her life forever
articles.standfirst: Years after divorce, her emotional reflection on their relationship has resurfaced
articles.summary: Years after divorce, her emotional reflection on their relationship has resurfaced
articles.body:
Long before Tom Brady and Gisele Bundchen became one of the most famous couples in sports and entertainment, their relationship began with a simple blind date and a shared vision of what their future could look like.

Bundchen was already one of the biggest names in fashion when she met Brady through mutual friend Ed Razek .

At the time, the Brazilian model was 26 years old and said she felt ready for the next chapter of her life, one centered around marriage and starting a family.

Looking back during a 2023 interview with Vanity Fair, Bundchen explained that her priorities were clear when Brady entered her world: “When I met Tom, I was 26 years old, and I wanted a family. I felt so ready.”

The relationship quickly developed, with Brady and Bundchen eventually marrying in 2009.

Together, they built a family while balancing the demands of two high-profile careers, with Brady becoming an NFL icon and Bundchen continuing her success as one of the world’s most recognizable models.

Their marriage lasted 13 years before the couple finalized their divorce in October 2022, bringing an end to one of the most closely followed relationships in the public eye.

Gisele says paths eventually changed

While their separation generated widespread attention, Bundchen later explained that the breakup wasn't about one specific moment or disagreement. Instead, she described it as a gradual realization that their individual goals had evolved over time.

In her Vanity Fair interview, Bundchen said that the couple’s relationship began with the same hopes but eventually reached a point where they wanted different things.

“Sometimes you grow together; sometimes you grow apart," Bundchen said. "When I was 26 years old and he was 29 years old, we met, we wanted a family, we wanted things together. As time goes by, we realize that we just wanted different things, and now we have a choice to make.”

Her comments provided a more personal look at the challenges of maintaining a relationship while both people continue to grow and change.

Brady ’s commitment to football remained a defining part of his life, while Bundchen also focused on her own goals and identity beyond being a partner and mother.

Despite their divorce, Bundchen emphasized that the end of their marriage didn't erase the bond they shared.

“That doesn’t mean you don’t love the person," Gisele stated. "It just means that in order for you to be authentic and truly live the life that you want to live, you have to have somebody who can meet you in the middle, right? It’s a dance. It’s a balance.”

A love story that shaped both lives

The beginning of Brady and Bundchen ’s relationship was built around a shared desire for family and a future together. Although their journey eventually took them in separate directions, Bundchen ’s reflections showed that she still views those years as an important part of her life.

Their blind date became the starting point of a relationship that included marriage, children and countless public moments. Years later, Bundchen ’s words highlighted a more complicated reality that sometimes relationships can be meaningful and lasting while still changing over time.

articles.title: Troy Aikman weighs in on Fernando Mendoza's future as the Raiders' franchise quarterback
articles.standfirst: Aikman offers high praise for Fernando Mendoza after the Raiders rookie's preseason debut
articles.summary: Aikman offers high praise for Fernando Mendoza after the Raiders rookie's preseason debut
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders may have found the quarterback they hope can define their next era, and Troy Aikman believes Fernando Mendoza has the qualities needed to become that player.

Mendoza received an extended opportunity Thursday night as Las Vegas defeated the Houston Texans 22-20 in preseason action.

With Kirk Cousins among the starters who didn't play, rookie quarterback Mendoza took the first-team snaps and remained on the field throughout the opening half.

The No. 1 overall pick wasn't flawless. He completed 8 of 15 attempts for 86 yards, was sacked once and threw an interception that Houston's Wade Woodaz returned 80 yards for a touchdown. Still, Aikman wasn't discouraged by the mistake.

"I don't want to get too far ahead of myself, but he has shown me already, in such a short time, that this young man is capable of being a really great player in this league,” Aikman said during the broadcast.

Aikman's endorsement emphasized that quarterbacks entering the NFL must demonstrate leadership and a willingness to handle the small details that separate successful players from talented ones.

Aikman sees the pieces for Mendoza to thrive

Aikman also sees reasons for optimism around Mendoza . He highlighted head coach Klint Kubiak's offensive coaching and identified tight end Brock Bowers and running back Ashton Jeanty as two foundational pieces who could help the young quarterback.

“I think that with Klint Kubiak, he’s going to have good coaching on the offensive side of the ball,” said Aikman .

“I do like some of these young players that they have. Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers . I mean, that’s a pretty good place to start to have those two cornerstone pieces offensively.”

The Raiders still have work to do, particularly when it comes to protecting Mendoza and improving their receiving corps. But Aikman doesn't believe every weakness needs to be solved immediately.

That patience could prove important. Mendoza isn't guaranteed to open the regular season as the starter, with veteran Cousins still in the quarterback picture.

Nevertheless, the rookie's long-term importance is obvious after Las Vegas made him the first selection in the 2026 NFL Draft. He arrived after leading Indiana to an undefeated national championship season and winning the Heisman Trophy.

Mendoza also understands that development won't happen overnight. After Thursday's game, he explained that his preparation hadn't changed despite knowing he'd receive the entire first half. He approached the opportunity as he would any start, focusing on preparation and learning.

articles.title: Has Fernando Mendoza done enough to challenge Kirk Cousins for the starting job with the Raiders?
articles.standfirst: The rookie quarterback still has a clear chance of being the No. 1 option for the season opener
articles.summary: The rookie quarterback still has a clear chance of being the No. 1 option for the season opener
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders may not have officially named their Week 1 starting quarterback, but head coach Klint Kubiak's latest comments suggest the competition is not over yet. And that could be welcome news for Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick who continues to gain valuable experience during his first NFL preseason.

While veteran Kirk Cousins remains the favorite to open the regular season under center when the Raiders host the Miami Dolphins on September 13, Kubiak once again declined to announce a starter following Las Vegas' preseason matchup against the Houston Texans.

His refusal to make a decision public has fueled speculation that Mendoza still has a legitimate chance to earn the job before Week 1. Fernando's second preseason appearance was far from perfect, but it may have provided exactly the type of experience the Raiders believe their young quarterback needs.

Mendoza needs to continue improving

After an impressive debut in which he looked poised and confident, Mendoza encountered his first real NFL adversity against Houston. The rookie completed 8 of 15 passes for 86 yards and threw his first interception, a mistake that Texans linebacker Wade Woodaz returned for a touchdown. The play highlighted some of the challenges Mendoza will face as he adjusts to the speed and complexity of professional defenses.

For Kubiak , however, the interception was less important than what comes next. When asked Friday what Mendoza needs most to continue improving, the rookie head coach delivered a simple answer. “Reps,” Kubiak said. “I know that's a short answer, but that's the truth.”

That response speaks volumes about how the organization views Mendoza's future. The Raiders are not focused solely on one preseason throw or one difficult night. Instead, they are evaluating how quickly the rookie learns from mistakes and whether he can continue progressing through experience.

Kubiak has avoided declaring Cousins the starter

The development process extends beyond Mendoza. Kubiak is navigating his first season as an NFL head coach, offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko is in his first year calling plays, and rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. is also learning on the fly. Growing pains are expected throughout the organization.

Although Cousins brings years of NFL experience and stability to a team undergoing major changes, Kubiak has consistently avoided declaring him the Week 1 starter. Asked again about the situation, the coach explained that competition remains valuable for every player on the roster.

“I just don't think it ever benefits a player to know they have a spot secured,” Kubiak said. That philosophy leaves the door open for Mendoza , even if the rookie currently trails Cousins in the battle for the starting role. One concern often raised with young quarterbacks is how they continue developing if they are not receiving starter-level practice repetitions.

Kubiak acknowledged that challenge but emphasized that the Raiders have a plan in place should Mendoza begin the season as a backup. “It’s a great point,” Kubiak said. Those comments underscore just how highly the Raiders view Mendoza's long-term potential. Even if Cousins starts against Miami, the organization appears committed to accelerating the rookie's development through film study, coaching sessions, and every available practice opportunity.

articles.title: Maxx Crosby takes Fernando Mendoza under his wing despite his own uncertainty regarding his future with the Raiders
articles.standfirst: The Raiders veteran showed the kind of leadership Las Vegas needs as its No. 1 pick endured a difficult preseason outing
articles.summary: The Raiders veteran showed the kind of leadership Las Vegas needs as its No. 1 pick endured a difficult preseason outing
articles.body:
M axx Crosby may have plenty of questions surrounding his own future with the Las Vegas Raiders , but the veteran defensive star is still making sure rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza knows he has support inside the locker room.

That was evident during Las Vegas' preseason meeting with the Houston Texans , when Mendoza endured one of the toughest moments of his young NFL career.

The No. 1 overall pick threw an interception that Houston's Wade Woodaz returned 80 yards for a touchdown, putting the Raiders in an early hole.

Mendoza completed 8 of 15 passes for 86 yards and the interception during his five series before leaving the game at halftime. The Raiders eventually recovered to win 22-20, but the rookie's difficult first half was an important test of how he would respond to adversity.

Crosby , however, was there for him. As Mendoza described the conversation: “It was something along the lines of: ‘We got your back. Let’s go next play.’ To hear that from a team captain is very inspiring.”

The rookie clearly appreciates the influence of one of the most established figures in the Raiders organization.

“Maxx is a great team captain and great team leader, and he’s always encouraging that resilience because adversity is going to happen,” Mendoza said.

That relationship could become particularly important as Mendoza adjusts to the demands of professional football. While veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins remains a major part of the quarterback conversation, Crosby has spent years serving as one of the franchise's most recognizable leaders.

Crosby's future adds another layer to the relationship

The unusual part of Crosby's mentorship is that his own position with the Raiders has been anything but certain.

Las Vegas agreed to trade the five-time Pro Bowl defensive end to the Baltimore Ravens during the offseason in a deal that would have sent two first-round selections to the Raiders.

However, Baltimore backed out after Crosby's physical raised medical concerns, leaving the defensive star back in Las Vegas.

That episode means Crosby knows firsthand how quickly circumstances can change in the NFL.

The Raiders ultimately kept one of their most important players, but another trade remains possible if the team's season goes poorly and Crosby demonstrates that his knee is no longer a concern. That possibility makes his commitment to helping Mendoza even more notable.

Crosby's logic is straightforward: if he is going to succeed in Las Vegas, the franchise needs to develop the quarterback who could become its long-term answer.

Mendoza's performance against Houston showed both promise and areas that need work. Before the interception, he had connected with Jalen Nailor on a 22-yard pass and later found Malik Benson for a key third-down completion.

The Raiders' coaching staff also remains cautious about handing Mendoza the starting job. Head coach Klint Kubiak has not officially named his Week 1 quarterback, with Cousins still expected to have a strong chance of starting.

For Mendoza , that uncertainty makes every preseason opportunity valuable.

Crosby's message, meanwhile, provides a reminder that development in the NFL is rarely linear. Mistakes will happen, particularly for a rookie quarterback facing professional defenses for the first time.

The Raiders need Mendoza to improve on the field, but they also need the kind of veteran leadership Crosby demonstrated on the sideline.

Whether Crosby ultimately remains in Las Vegas for the entire season is still unclear. But for now, his message to Mendoza represents exactly what a young quarterback needs to hear: one bad play does not have to define the next one.

articles.title: Klint Kubiak keeps starting QB position open between Fernando Mendoza and Kirk Cousins: “I don't want anyone to get too comfortable”
articles.standfirst: The veteran and No.1 pick are battling for control of Las Vegas’ offense before Week 1
articles.summary: The veteran and No.1 pick are battling for control of Las Vegas’ offense before Week 1
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders expected their quarterback competition to be one of the biggest storylines of the 2026 offseason, and head coach Klint Kubiak has made one thing clear that nobody has done enough to claim the job yet.

With veteran Kirk Cousins and No.1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza competing for the starting role, the Raiders entered preseason with two very different options at the most important position on the field. Cousins offers experience and stability, while Mendoza represents the future of the franchise.

But after Mendoza ’s first preseason start against the Houston Texans , Kubiak refused to indicate that the rookie had moved ahead or that Cousins had secured the position.

“We got another week. I don’t want anyone to be comfortable in their job,” Kubiak said. “It should always be that way for all positions. So, let’s keep going.”

The message from Las Vegas’ head coach has kept the pressure on both quarterbacks as the team prepares for its regular-season opener against the Miami Dolphins .

Mendoza received the starting opportunity against Houston and played the entire first half, completing 8 of 15 passes for 86 yards. The former Indiana quarterback also threw his first NFL interception, which was returned for a touchdown by Texans linebacker Wade Woodaz .

Despite the mistake, the rookie remains in contention for the starting role. Cousins , meanwhile, watched the opening half from the sideline before Aidan O’Connell took over in the second half.

The veteran joined the Raiders in April on a five-year, $172 million contract, a commitment that appeared to position him as the early favorite. However, Kubiak ’s approach suggests the organization is willing to evaluate every option before making a final decision.

Mendoza focused on growth after first NFL start

The rookie quarterback understood the importance of his first preseason start and viewed it as another step in his development.

“Coach Kubiak outlined for the team what the plan was going to be with the starters, essentially for Weeks one, two and three of the preseason, [and] to keep it internally,” Mendoza said.

“That was something I knew going into the game was going to be a great experience as a first start in the NFL preseason, which is always the next step.”

While the interception was a difficult moment, Mendoza focused on improving his mechanics and decision-making as he adjusts to the speed of professional football.

“Maybe stepping up in the pocket,” Mendoza said when asked what he could improve. “Maybe stepping side to side to give [me] a little bit more time and try to best serve my teammates.”

The Raiders ’ quarterback decision carries significant consequences. Starting Cousins would provide a proven veteran presence, while choosing Mendoza would accelerate the development of the player the franchise selected first overall.

Aidan O’Connell ’s strong preseason performance has also given Las Vegas another option, although the main competition remains between Cousins and Mendoza .

The Raiders still have time before Week 1, but Kubiak ’s comments have ensured the battle remains open. Instead of handing the job to the veteran or rushing the rookie into action, Las Vegas appears determined to let performance decide.

articles.standfirst: The NFL legend marks son Jack’s 19th birthday by reflecting on the moment that transformed his life and celebrating the young man he has become
articles.summary: The NFL legend marks son Jack’s 19th birthday by reflecting on the moment that transformed his life and celebrating the young man he has become
articles.body:
T om Brady has never been short of defining moments. Seven Super Bowl victories, countless records and a career that established him as one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history have given Brady a résumé that few athletes can approach.

But for the former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers star, one particular date carries a meaning that has nothing to do with football. August 22, 2007, was the day his eldest son, Jack, was born.

Nineteen years later, Brady used the occasion to look back at the moment that changed his life, sharing an emotional birthday tribute to Jack on social media. The post reflected not only on his son's growth but also on how much fatherhood has meant to him since becoming a parent.

"Happy 19th birthday, Jack!" Brady wrote in the caption. "Aug 22, 2007 is a day I’ll never forget, because that’s when you showed up and stole my heart (and my sleep … and my patience … hahahaha). The significance of the date goes beyond Jack's birth. Brady and actress Bridget Moynahan had ended their relationship in late 2006 after roughly three years together. Their split was followed by news in February 2007 that Moynahan was pregnant with Brady's child.

At the time, Brady was also beginning a relationship with Gisele Bundchen , making an already complicated personal situation the subject of enormous public attention.

Brady was reluctant to discuss the circumstances publicly. During a 2007 Patriots media session, he acknowledged that his personal life had presented new challenges while making clear that he wanted to focus on football.

What followed, however, was the beginning of a long-term co-parenting relationship involving Brady and Moynahan .

Moynahan has previously spoken about how the pair ultimately created a supportive environment around Jack, with both of their subsequent partners playing roles in his upbringing.

Jack has developed his own sporting identity

While Jack has grown up surrounded by elite athletes, he has not simply attempted to copy his father's career.

The 19-year-old has developed a particular interest in basketball, and Brady has frequently shared glimpses of his son's ability on the court.

His latest birthday tribute included photographs of Jack playing basketball, while Brady also joked about his son's athletic advantages over his father.

The difference in physical profiles is certainly noticeable. Brady built his career around anticipation, accuracy and decision-making rather than explosive athleticism, while Jack has developed into a considerably taller athlete.

Brady previously joked about his son's jumping ability, telling the Fortune Global Forum in 2024: "Unfortunately he jumps as high as I do," before adding that he expected Jack to become a strong player as he grew.

The teenager also recently reached another major milestone when he graduated from high school in June. Brady and Moynahan were both present for the occasion, providing another example of the family coming together to celebrate Jack.

Brady's pride in his eldest son has become increasingly visible as Jack has moved toward adulthood.

Rather than insisting that he follow in his father's footsteps, Brady has repeatedly emphasised that his role is to support whatever direction his children choose.

That philosophy extends to his other two children, Benjamin and Vivian , whom he shares with former wife Bündchen. Brady has spoken about wanting his children to find purpose and happiness rather than simply reproducing his own extraordinary sporting career.

For Jack, that future could potentially involve basketball, although his plans remain his own.

For Brady , meanwhile, August 22 is likely to remain one of the most important dates of his life. Nearly two decades after the circumstances surrounding Jack's arrival changed his world, the former quarterback is now watching his son enter adulthood.

And if Brady's latest tribute is any indication, the memories of that life-changing day remain just as powerful as ever.

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty’s potential replacement is already making a strong case to be the Raiders’ No. 1 back
articles.standfirst: The situation is potentially significant for the Las Vegas offense
articles.summary: The situation is potentially significant for the Las Vegas offense
articles.body:
T he Las Vegas Raiders may have been dealt a major blow Sunday when running back Ashton Jeanty suffered an apparent right leg injury at practice, but they may also have a rookie ready to step into the spotlight. Mike Washington Jr. has quietly emerged as one of the most impressive players of Las Vegas' preseason , and if Jeanty is forced to miss significant time, the rookie could suddenly find himself carrying a much larger portion of the Raiders' offense.

Jeanty, the No. 6 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, did not put weight on his right leg after landing awkwardly while diving for a pass, according to reports. Trainers helped him from the field, and the Raiders subsequently gathered for a team prayer. The organization had not immediately provided an update on the severity of the injury.

The situation is potentially significant for a Las Vegas offense counting on Jeanty to build on an impressive rookie campaign. The 22-year-old finished his first NFL season with 1,321 scrimmage yards and 10 total touchdowns, establishing himself as one of the central pieces of the Raiders' offensive attack.

Washington could be asked to fill some enormous shoes

And based on what he has shown so far, the Raiders have reason to believe he is capable. Washington has impressed during his first two preseason appearances, demonstrating the combination of size, explosiveness and versatility that could make him much more than a temporary replacement.

At 6-foot-2 and 228 pounds, Washington has the physical profile of a featured NFL running back. His résumé also suggests that his preseason success is not coming out of nowhere. The Utica, New York , native played his final college season at Arkansas in 2025 after spending one year at New Mexico State and three seasons at Buffalo.

Across his college career, he recorded 587 rushing attempts for 2,914 yards and 26 touchdowns while adding 73 receptions for 470 yards and three receiving touchdowns. His lone season with Arkansas was particularly impressive.

Washington started all 12 games and rushed 167 times for 1,070 yards and eight touchdowns. He averaged 6.4 yards per carry, a remarkable figure that ranked second in the SEC and ninth nationally. He also caught 28 passes for 226 yards and another touchdown. That production earned him Second-Team All-SEC honors.

The Raiders clearly saw something in Washington

They brought him into the organization, but his preseason performances have accelerated the conversation around his potential role. With Jeanty potentially sidelined, Washington could be the next man up, and perhaps more than that.

The Raiders' running back room also includes Dylan Laube, Roman Hemby and veteran Dare Ogunbowale, while Connor Heyward and Patrick Gurd provide fullback options. There are other possibilities for replacing Jeanty's touches, but Washington appears to have separated himself through his combination of talent and recent production. His emergence could be particularly valuable for an offense still developing its identity.

A featured running back needs to do more than simply carry the football. He has to contribute in the passing game, protect the quarterback, handle different running concepts and remain productive when defenses know he is getting the ball. Washington's college résumé suggests he can do all of those things.

His 73 career receptions also demonstrate that he is comfortable catching passes, while his size gives the Raiders a powerful option between the tackles. The 6.4 yards-per-carry average he posted in the SEC shows that he also possesses the explosiveness to turn routine opportunities into substantial gains. The timing of his emergence could hardly be more important.

articles.title: Tom Brady won't make Raiders any better unless he makes major decision, according to Mike Florio
articles.standfirst: Florio questions whether Brady can help transform Las Vegas while balancing responsibilities away from the Raiders
articles.summary: Florio questions whether Brady can help transform Las Vegas while balancing responsibilities away from the Raiders
articles.body:
T om Brady 's involvement with the Las Vegas Raiders has once again become a talking point, with NBC's Mike Florio questioning whether the seven-time Super Bowl champion can have the desired impact without becoming more deeply committed to the organization.

Brady joined the Raiders ' ownership group in 2023 and has remained involved in football operations despite not serving as a traditional full-time executive.

That arrangement has prompted debate about how much influence he should have over the franchise's most important decisions and whether his other professional commitments prevent him from being fully immersed in Las Vegas .

Florio believes at least one rival team is hoping the current arrangement remains unchanged.

“I basically got a tongue in cheek request from another team. ‘Stop talking about the Brady stuff. Stop talking about it,'” Florio said on PFT Live on Friday.

The request, according to Florio , came with a blunt explanation for why an opposing organization would prefer Brady to remain in his current role.

“Why? ‘He’s not going to make them any better, as long as he’s doing all this other sh*t. So, let him, let him keep doing what he’s doing. Let him think that he’s in a position to turn this thing around, because he’s not,’” Florio said the team representative told him.

The unnamed representative then contrasted Brady 's approach with former NFL quarterback Matt Ryan , who moved into a full-time broadcasting career after retiring from football.

“‘I’m more worried about Matt Ryan,’ I was told, ‘than I am Tom Brady, because Matt Ryan, right, he loaded up the truck and moved to Atlanta," Florio added. "He’s there. He didn’t try to do both jobs. He’s all in, all the time. You got to be all in, all the time to be effective.'”

Influence extends beyond physical presence

Florio 's criticism is not necessarily based on the idea that Brady has no influence in Las Vegas. In fact, reports have suggested the opposite. Brady has been linked to several major football decisions since becoming part of the Raiders' ownership structure.

One of the most notable examples involved Chip Kelly , who became the team's offensive coordinator after developing a relationship with Brady that dates back more than a decade.

Kelly and Brady reportedly worked together during the 2025 season, including preparation for a matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers .

An NFL social-media post discussing their collaboration was reportedly deleted after briefly stating that the pair had been working “closely together” during the week.

That remote involvement has become part of the broader discussion about Brady 's role. Florio 's argument is that having influence without being fully present could leave the Raiders in an awkward middle ground.

The issue has become even more prominent because of Fernando Mendoza , the quarterback selected first overall by the Raiders .

Florio recently criticized the idea of keeping Mendoza on the sideline for an extended period, arguing that Las Vegas needs to maximize the value of such a significant investment.

“I’m not even going to be that wishy washy about it. I don’t like the idea of the number one overall pick in the draft not playing,” Florio said.

“The Raiders need a spark. The Raiders need to get a return on their investment.

"And the sooner Fernando Mendoza plays, the sooner the game slows down. I hate to think that this number one approach to sitting Fernando Mendoza for maybe a full season is simply because that’s what Tommy wants.

"I also hate to think that Tommy wants it because he didn’t play as a rookie. I didn’t play as a rookie, so that must be the right approach for everyone…”

Florio believes Brady 's own experience as a young quarterback should not necessarily dictate what happens with Mendoza : “Just because it works specifically for him, doesn’t mean it’s the right way in today’s NFL.

"I think in today’s NFL, if you’re going to use that number one overall pick on a quarterback, you better get that quarterback ready to play. He better be a guy who you think can play right away. If he’s not, you need to pick somebody else, you need to trade out of that spot.”

The larger question is therefore not whether Brady cares about the Raiders . His involvement in football matters suggests that he does. Instead, Florio is challenging whether Brady 's current structure gives him enough time and authority to make a meaningful difference.

For a franchise attempting to change its fortunes, that distinction could become increasingly important.

If Brady wants to influence the Raiders ' direction on a deeper level, Florio 's argument is straightforward: he may ultimately need to choose the Raiders over some of his other commitments and become “all in, all the time.”

Whether that happens could have a significant impact on how much influence Brady ultimately has over the Raiders ' next chapter.

articles.title: Injury to Ashton Jeanty could change Raiders' plans and 'send' Maxx Crosby to the Cowboys
articles.standfirst: A failed offseason deal may not be the end of the story if Las Vegas chooses to chase premium draft capital
articles.summary: A failed offseason deal may not be the end of the story if Las Vegas chooses to chase premium draft capital
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders suddenly have another reason to think about the future after Ashton Jeanty ’s ankle injury, and one proposed solution involves a move that would dramatically reshape both sides of the ball.

Cowboys writer Clarence Hill Jr. has urged Las Vegas to reopen trade discussions involving Maxx Crosby , arguing that the Raiders could send their All-Pro pass rusher to the Dallas Cowboys and begin positioning themselves for Ohio State star Jeremiah Smith in the 2027 NFL Draft.

“With Jeanty hurt, the Raiders might as well trade Maxx Crosby to the Dallas cowboys now and work on getting Jeremiah Smith at the top of the draft,” Hill wrote on X.

The suggestion comes after Jeanty suffered what has been reported as a sprained ankle, creating immediate concern around an offense already facing questions at wide receiver.

Trading Crosby would be an enormous decision, but Dallas has already demonstrated serious interest.

The Cowboys reportedly made three attempts to acquire him during the offseason, with one offer including the No.12 overall pick in the 2026 draft and a 2027 second-round selection.

Baltimore eventually offered two first-round picks, although that proposed deal collapsed after Crosby failed a physical.

Cowboys could get another chance at Crosby

With Baltimore no longer involved, the possibility of Dallas returning to the table has resurfaced. Crosby remains the highest-paid player on the Raiders ’ roster, carrying a $35.79 million cap charge.

Moving him would cost Las Vegas one of the league’s best defensive players, but it could also deliver the premium draft capital needed to accelerate a long-term rebuild.

The Cowboys have already strengthened their pass rush by adding Rashan Gary , although Crosby would provide an entirely different level of established production and could become the centerpiece of their defensive front.

Dallas’ previous willingness to surrender major draft assets also makes it an obvious destination if Las Vegas decides to listen before the November 10 trade deadline.

Jeremiah Smith could transform Raiders offense

The other half of the proposal centers on Smith , one of the most highly regarded players expected to be available in the 2027 draft.

Smith is primarily an elite wide receiver rather than a conventional replacement for Jeanty, although the original proposal imagines Klint Kubiak finding creative ways to use him from the backfield while also making him the Raiders ’ No.1 receiving weapon.

That could be particularly attractive for quarterback Fernando Mendoza , who would gain a potentially dominant target as Las Vegas attempts to build its offense around younger talent.

Kubiak has already expressed disappointment with his receivers following their performance against Houston, adding further weight to the argument that Las Vegas could eventually prioritize an explosive playmaker.

“If this truly is a precursor to how their actual season will go, it should be Jeremiah Smith they look to draft already in 2027,” Marissa Myers wrote for TWSN.

None of that means a Crosby trade is imminent. There is currently no indication that the Raiders are actively shopping him. Still, Jeanty ’s injury has reopened a larger question about Las Vegas’ timeline.

If the season begins moving in the wrong direction, turning Crosby into premium draft capital could become one of the biggest decisions of the NFL trade deadline.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza enters the final stretch of preseason still trailing Kirk Cousins in the quarterback battle
articles.standfirst: The Raiders will open the season at home against Miami, but first they have their final preseason game against the 49ers
articles.summary: The Raiders will open the season at home against Miami, but first they have their final preseason game against the 49ers
articles.body:
Through the first two preseason games, the Las Vegas Raiders are still searching for their footing, splitting action with veteran Kirk Cousins starting the opener and rookie sensation Fernando Mendoza taking the reins for the second.

Head coach Klint Kubiak has been clear that the veteran Cousins will command the offense as the Week 1 starter against Miami , a calculated strategy signed off in the offseason to shield Mendoza from being rushed immediately into the pro fire.

This patient approach mirrors the developmental blueprints of legendary signal-callers like Tom Brady , Aaron Rodgers , and Patrick Mahomes , all of whom spent their rookie campaigns observing from the clipboard rather than facing bullets right away.

Fernando Mendoza Faces Growing Pains in Preseason

During Week 2 of the preseason, a wave of 15 rookie quarterbacks saw live action , with the first overall pick drawing plenty of spotlight as he navigates the massive competitive leap from college to the professional ranks.

Going up against the Houston Texans , Mendoza finished his first start completing 8-of-15 passes for 86 yards , though his defining moment came when an early misfire turned into an 80-year pick-six by linebacker Wade Woodaz on the opening possession.

Facing one of the stingiest defensive units in the league, a squad that ranked No. 1 in yards allowed per game , provided an invaluable crash course in reading complex NFL coverages.

While the early turnover put Las Vegas in a deep hole, Mendoza showed resilience by engineering drives and leaning on tight end Ian Thomas and running back Dylan Laube before halftime, proving that a slow preseason progression is completely normal.

Building a New Era in Las Vegas for the Long Haul

The Raiders have zero intentions of accelerating Mendoza's timeline because the franchise is firmly committed to laying a sustainable foundation under a new general manager and coaching staff, pairing their young cornerstone with standout playmakers like running back Ashton Jeanty and tight end Brock Bowers .

For an organization that has endured 18 losing seasons and just two playoff appearances since their last Super Bowl trip in 2002 , the excitement around the future remains sky-high regardless of how early growing pains manifest.

Las Vegas will officially launch the regular season at home against the Miami Dolphins on September 13 , followed by consecutive road battles against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2 and the New Orleans Saints in Week 3

articles.title: Tom Brady sends ‘terrifying’ message to the women who could replace Gisele Bundchen
articles.standfirst: Children and work dominate his life as he reflects on a difficult final season.
articles.summary: Children and work dominate his life as he reflects on a difficult final season.
articles.body:
Tom Brady spent more than two decades structuring almost every part of his life around football. Retirement has changed the setting, but not necessarily the pace.

The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback says his schedule remains packed with work, business commitments and time with his children, leaving little room for much else.

“I don't have much time for a personal life or much time for myself, but I love working and I love my kids,” Brady told PEOPLE.

That admission comes years after his 2022 divorce from Gisele Bundchen , a split that prompted widespread speculation over whether his decision to continue playing football had strained their marriage.

Brady has never reduced the breakup to one cause, and Bundchen has also pushed back on the idea that football alone explained what happened.

Still, the 49-year-old has acknowledged that his final season came during an unusually difficult period away from the field.

Priorities shifted at the end of career

Speaking on The Herd with Colin Cowherd, Brady reflected on why retirement finally made sense after 23 NFL seasons.

“I had 23 years of [football] so I didn’t think I was missing anything, retiring,” Brady said. “I felt like I always had a goal... 45.

"I was 45 years old, I wanted to spend time with my kids, I felt like, okay, now it’s time for me to be at all my kids’ games. They’ve been to enough of their dad’s games.”

He also admitted that his final year didn't end the way he would have wanted.

“I felt like I owed to my teammates and coaches to give them everything I had,” Brady said. “I wish it could have been a little bit better at the end. But it was just a unique situation and a unique year for me.”

That season coincided with his divorce from Bundchen , who later told Vanity Fair that the reasons behind their split were more complicated than outside speculation suggested.

“Things were not so black and white,” Bundchen admitted.

Brady says staying busy still gives him purpose Retirement has not brought much slowing down.

“I like to be busy and try to really stay fulfilled in the things I'm doing, so I'm working on some really cool projects and I'm involved with some great teams of people that are doing some really positive things,” Brady added.

He has remained closely tied to football through media work and his ownership stake in the Las Vegas Raiders , while also becoming increasingly involved in business ventures.

That includes taking a personal interest in Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza .

Brady recently bought a one-of-one rookie card featuring Mendoza ’s first NFL autograph, calling the purchase an investment in what he hopes will be a successful era for Las Vegas.

“I know how hard he works,” Brady said. “He's got a great family and he's coming to a great environment for success.”

Football may no longer consume every Sunday, but Brady ’s priorities remain familiar. The difference now is that he appears more willing to admit just how little space that leaves for anything else.

articles.standfirst: The football legend has taken a humble approach while highlighting the best QBs in league history.
articles.summary: The football legend has taken a humble approach while highlighting the best QBs in league history.
articles.body:
For opposing fans who thought that Tom Brady would just ride off into the sunset without a word following a 23-year NFL career , they couldn't have been more wrong. And they clearly weren't paying attention to how Brady operates.

Aside from his post-playing contract with Fox Sports , as their lead NFL color commentator, Brady has practically stayed in the spotlight without a hitch through various methods . One of those is his personal social media accounts, which allow him to say trendy and keep his fans up to date with what's going on in his life.

Tom Brady mentions Patrick Mahomes and Lamar Jackson in perfect QB list

This week was no different in that regard, but Brady got people talking in a different way this time around. In a video going around on social media, Brady built what he believes would be a " perfect NFL quarterback ". Surprisingly, there was no room for Brady himself as one of the QBs .

Pocket Presence: Andrew Luck

Throw Power: Aaron Rodgers

Throw Accuracy: Drew Brees

Identifying Coverage: Peyton Manning

Playmaking: Patrick Mahomes

While running through his picks, Brady couldn't help but also get in a dig at Eli Manning , saying that he would be the pick for having a " lucky gene ". Manning famously beat Brady in two separate Super Bowls while with the New York Giants .

articles.title: The controversial advice a former NFL player gave Fernando Mendoza in Las Vegas: “Go to a strip club”
articles.standfirst: Breiden Fehoko believes the Raiders rookie needs to loosen up as he adjusts to life in the NFL
articles.summary: Breiden Fehoko believes the Raiders rookie needs to loosen up as he adjusts to life in the NFL
articles.body:
F ernando Mendoza has quickly developed a reputation for being one of the most polished young quarterbacks in football, but one former NFL player believes the Las Vegas Raiders rookie could benefit from becoming a little less serious.

Former Los Angeles Chargers defensive tackle Breiden Fehoko offered Mendoza some unusually blunt advice after watching the No. 1 overall pick struggle during the Raiders ' preseason matchup with the Houston Texans .

Mendoza played the entire first half of Las Vegas ' 22-20 comeback victory on Aug. 20, completing 8 of 15 passes for 86 yards.

His night included an 80-yard interception return for a touchdown by Texans linebacker Wade Woodaz , an error that helped Houston establish a commanding early advantage.

The performance was a difficult one for a rookie facing an increasingly high level of expectation. Mendoza had shown flashes in his preseason debut against the Arizona Cardinals , including throwing his first preseason touchdown, but the Texans provided a much tougher test.

Fehoko acknowledged that Mendoza still has work to do, while also pointing toward the physical tools and potential that made him the first selection in the 2026 NFL Draft.

But it was Mendoza's personality away from the field that attracted the former defensive lineman's attention.

“My only thing for Fernando Mendoza is we got to cool it on the interviews, bro. Like if we can just, and he’s like, ‘Yeah, uh, thank you, Mr. Buck,’ and ‘Yeah, I’m so grateful to be…’ Like, okay, Fernando, I get it. You did your thing in college; you were grateful, God is good, God is amazing, cool. But my big dog, we got to play quarterback now. You feel me? Like, them interviews, I get it, you’re a happy man, like go get with Maxx Crosby, go to a strip club, like lighten up, you know what I’m saying? So that’s my thoughts on Fernando Mendoza. I think he’s going to be a good player,” Fehoko explained on The Breiden Fehoko Show.

Mendoza's polished image is part of who he is

Fehoko's comments highlight an interesting contrast between how Mendoza presents himself and the more relaxed personality some former players believe is necessary to survive the NFL.

The Raiders quarterback has become known for his exceptionally careful and respectful answers during media appearances.

Rather than treating that as a manufactured persona, however, Mendoza's family has indicated that his communication skills have been developed over many years.

“People might think it’s fake, but it’s 100 percent him,” said Alberto Mendoza, per The Athletic’s Chris Vannini . “It’s greatly due to our parents. They taught us how to speak to people, how to carry ourselves, how to act in a professional manner.”

Mendoza himself has also discussed deliberately working on his communication. At the NFL Combine, he explained that he had taken speech classes, studied communication techniques and focused heavily on becoming a better leader.

“So, let me get really good at speaking. I’ve always taken speech classes; I’ve always looked at YouTube videos on how to communicate, you know, how to be a better leader, a huge reader as well. So, with that, it’s developed senses where people like all this guy’s ChatGPT, but I’ve been able to connect with my teammates really well and not in a ChatGPT scenario,” Mendoza told Raiders general manager John Spytek.

That background makes Fehoko's criticism less straightforward than simply telling a young quarterback to change who he is. Mendoza's composure and professionalism are qualities that could ultimately serve him well in a demanding leadership position.

The bigger question is whether he can translate those qualities into consistent performances on the field.

Against Houston , the Raiders trailed 20-3 before rallying for the victory. Mendoza was finished after halftime, while the comeback was completed by the rest of the quarterback room and offense.

The rookie will now have another opportunity to respond before the regular season. The Raiders ' preseason schedule concludes against the San Francisco 49ers , giving Mendoza one more chance to build confidence and demonstrate that the Houston performance was simply part of the learning curve.

For now, Fehoko's unusual suggestion is better understood as a call for Mendoza to relax rather than a serious prescription for how the rookie should spend his free time.

The first overall pick has already shown that he takes his responsibilities seriously. His next challenge is proving that his polished approach can coexist with the improvisation, resilience and confidence required of an NFL quarterback.

And while “go to a strip club” is certainly not conventional quarterback advice, Fehoko's underlying message is much simpler: Mendoza needs to loosen up, enjoy the experience and keep learning as he makes the enormous jump from college football to the NFL.

articles.title: Report claims the Raiders may have “traded” Fernando Mendoza for Dante Moore
articles.standfirst: Las Vegas reportedly weighed a higher-upside Oregon quarterback before settling on the Heisman winner
articles.summary: Las Vegas reportedly weighed a higher-upside Oregon quarterback before settling on the Heisman winner
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders ultimately made Fernando Mendoza the centerpiece of their quarterback plans, selecting the Indiana star with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.

But a new report suggests the decision may not have been as straightforward as it appeared, with Oregon quarterback Dante Moore reportedly attracting serious attention from the franchise.

According to draft insider Todd McShay , the Raiders had not completely settled on Mendoza during the evaluation process.

Their internal debate reportedly involved choosing between a quarterback who appeared more prepared to contribute immediately and another prospect whose long-term potential was considered even greater.

“From my intel, they hadn’t made a decision,” he said on the Brandon Walker College Football Show. “It was going to be a very difficult one because Mendoza was more ready. Now, Dante Moore ’s ceiling was higher.”

The intriguing part of the story is that Moore never actually entered the 2026 draft. The Oregon quarterback announced in January that he would return to the Ducks for another season, removing one of the most highly regarded quarterbacks from the draft pool.

That decision helped clear the path for Mendoza , who had emerged as the overwhelming favorite to go first overall.

Las Vegas eventually made the Indiana quarterback its choice, and the Raiders officially signed him to a four-year rookie contract worth a reported $57.27 million fully guaranteed.

Why the Raiders were reportedly tempted by Moore's upside

The contrast between the two quarterbacks helps explain why the reported debate was so significant.

Mendoza entered the draft with an extraordinary résumé. He finished his final college season with 3,535 passing yards, 41 touchdowns and only six interceptions while completing 72% of his attempts.

He led Indiana to an undefeated national championship season and became the first Heisman Trophy winner in school history.

Moore's 2025 campaign was also impressive. He completed 71.8% of his passes for 3,565 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions as Oregon reached the College Football Playoff semifinals.

However, Moore had significantly less experience as a full-time starter, making his evaluation more dependent on projecting what he could become.

That appears to have been the attraction for Las Vegas. Mendoza represented the safer proposition, while Moore offered the possibility of becoming an even more dynamic quarterback several years down the road.

McShay went further when discussing what Moore could accomplish with another season at Oregon.

“Oregon is loaded talent-wise,” he added. “And I actually think a certain way that they’re even more loaded this year… So this is going to be a huge year for Dante. I’m telling you right now, man, Dante goes in as the number one guy. Dante might have been, had he elected to come out, the number one quarterback taken ahead of Fernando Mendoza.”

Moore's decision to remain in Eugene was therefore potentially significant for the Raiders ' draft plans. Had he entered the draft, Las Vegas may have faced a genuine decision between the two quarterbacks rather than simply taking Mendoza with the first selection.

For Moore , however, returning to Oregon offered another opportunity to chase a national championship. He explained that he wanted to continue developing and believed staying in college was the right move for him.

“There’s some unfinished goals,” Dan Lanning summed up the mood after his QB’s decision. “There’s some unfinished business. We’re a team that got so close the last two years.”

Mendoza now has the job of proving the Raiders chose correctly

There is no longer any mystery about which quarterback Las Vegas selected. Mendoza is officially a Raider , and the organization has invested heavily in his future.

The early stages of that transition have nevertheless provided some challenges. Mendoza has impressed at times during preseason, but he also threw an 80-yard interception return for a touchdown against Houston, finishing that outing 8-of-15 for 86 yards.

The Raiders still defeated the Texans 22-20, but the performance demonstrated that the transition from college football's top level to the NFL will require patience.

The Raiders have also indicated that veteran Kirk Cousins remains part of the quarterback competition, meaning Mendoza is not automatically guaranteed to start Week 1.

That makes the McShay report particularly interesting in hindsight. Las Vegas may have preferred Mendoza because he was more prepared for the NFL, while believing Moore possessed greater developmental upside.

If Moore eventually becomes a top NFL quarterback after his additional season at Oregon, the Raiders' reported interest will look even more significant.

For now, though, Las Vegas has made its choice, and Mendoza has the opportunity to prove that the team did not settle for the safer option, but selected the quarterback who can ultimately lead the franchise back to contention.

articles.title: Tom Brady explains the true emotional reasons behind his partnership with Gucci
articles.standfirst: The seven-time Super Bowl champion is embracing a completely different kind of challenge away from football
articles.summary: The seven-time Super Bowl champion is embracing a completely different kind of challenge away from football
articles.body:
T om Brady has spent much of his life operating in environments where preparation, routine and control were essential.

From becoming one of the most decorated quarterbacks in NFL history to building a career in business and broadcasting after retirement, the 49-year-old has rarely been associated with stepping into unfamiliar territory.

That changed this year when Brady became part of Gucci's latest fashion story, including a headline-making runway appearance in New York and a new campaign for the Italian luxury house's fall-winter 2026 collection.

For Brady , however, the partnership appears to represent more than simply adding another major brand to his résumé.

In a recent interview with GQ, Brady explained that the attraction was partly the opportunity to challenge himself and move beyond what he already knew.

He acknowledged that fashion was not necessarily his primary world, even though he had long appreciated well-dressed men and had attended some of the industry's biggest events.

Brady said: "I’ve always paid attention to a degree. I’ve been to plenty of Met Galas in my life, and I’ve always enjoyed stylish men’s clothing and suits, but I played it by ear on this particular occasion. I don’t come in with any preconceived notions. I just kind of take the opportunity for what it is, and then go for it.”

That attitude goes some way toward explaining why Brady was willing to make such an unexpected appearance.

From the football field to the Gucci runway

Brady made his Gucci runway debut in May during designer Demna's first cruise show for the fashion house, staged dramatically in Times Square.

He walked in an all-black leather outfit, an image that was a long way removed from the suits and athletic gear associated with his football career.

The setting itself was extraordinary. Gucci transformed part of Times Square for the show, creating a spectacle that brought together major names from entertainment, fashion and sport.

Brady's appearance was particularly striking because of how unexpected it was: one of the NFL's most recognizable figures suddenly found himself walking a runway rather than standing on a football sideline.

His involvement has now gone beyond that one night. Brady is one of the stars of Gucci's fall-winter 2026 campaign, photographed by Michal Chelbin alongside figures including Alex Consani, EsDeeKid and Shawn Mendes.

For Brady , the experience has also challenged some of his own assumptions about fashion.

The former quarterback admitted that he had never previously worn leather-on-leather in the way he did for Gucci, but was surprised by how comfortable the clothing felt. He even compared some of the structure of the outfit to the familiar feeling of a football uniform.

That comparison is revealing. Brady's success throughout his sporting career was built around adapting to new situations while maintaining confidence in his preparation.

The Gucci experience appears to have given him another opportunity to apply that mindset outside football.

Rather than presenting himself as a fashion expert, Brady has approached the collaboration with curiosity. His comments suggest that the emotional appeal lies in doing something unfamiliar and accepting the uncertainty that comes with it.

That is particularly significant for an athlete who has already achieved almost everything possible in his original profession.

With seven Super Bowl victories and a record-setting NFL career behind him, Brady no longer needs to prove himself on a football field.

Instead, Gucci has offered him a different kind of test: being willing to look unfamiliar, experiment with his image and trust the creative process.

And that may ultimately be the real reason the partnership has appealed to Brady. It is less about reinventing himself completely and more about remaining open to experiences he might once have considered outside his comfort zone.

The former quarterback admitted that he had never previously worn leather-on-leather in the way he did for Gucci, but was surprised by how comfortable the clothing felt. He even compared some of the structure of the outfit to the familiar feeling of a football uniform.
That comparison is revealing. Brady's success throughout his sporting career was built around adapting to new situations while maintaining confidence in his preparation.
The Gucci experience appears to have given him another opportunity to apply that mindset outside football.

Rather than presenting himself as a fashion expert, Brady has approached the collaboration with curiosity. His comments suggest that the emotional appeal lies in doing something unfamiliar and accepting the uncertainty that comes with it.
That is particularly significant for an athlete who has already achieved almost everything possible in his original profession.
With seven Super Bowl victories and a record-setting NFL career behind him, Brady no longer needs to prove himself on a football field.
Instead, Gucci has offered him a different kind of test: being willing to look unfamiliar, experiment with his image and trust the creative process.

And that may ultimately be the real reason the partnership has appealed to Brady. It is less about reinventing himself completely and more about remaining open to experiences he might once have considered outside his comfort zone.

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty’s cryptic post sparks injury concerns among Las Vegas Raiders fans
articles.standfirst: The Raiders are waiting for answers, but Jeanty’s latest message has everyone talking.
articles.summary: The Raiders are waiting for answers, but Jeanty’s latest message has everyone talking.
articles.body:
The entire Las Vegas Raiders fan base held its breath recently after it was revealed that running back Ashton Jeanty had to be helped off the field after suffering a leg injury during practice. At first, many feared the worst and even thought he could miss the entire season.

The Raiders have yet to officially confirm the severity of the injury, although multiple reports indicate that Jeanty suffered only an ankle sprain . While the injury could force him to miss some games, it is not expected to threaten his season.

The running back has not spoken publicly about what happened, but he did share a cryptic message on Instagram. Jeanty posted a photo of himself kneeling alongside the Bible verse Romans 8:28.

“And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose,” the verse reads.

It remains unclear what Jeanty intended to convey with the message. It could be interpreted as thanking God for helping him avoid a more serious injury, or as a sign of faith that even this setback is part of a greater purpose. What is certain is that his return timeline will depend on the Raiders’ final evaluation.

Klint Kubiak provides positive update on Jeanty

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak typically does not reveal many details about injuries, but his comments regarding Jeanty provided an encouraging sign.

“Again, Ashton got hurt in practice, and the whole team took a knee. That says a lot about him being on the mend and counting on him,” Kubiak told reporters. “Really excited about getting him back. I’m a huge believer in the power of prayer.”

Jeanty enters this season with high expectations after being selected in the Top 10 of the Draft and being considered one of the most talented running backs to come out of college in recent years . His impact will be crucial for a Las Vegas offense that could face major challenges if it is forced to move forward without its top weapon in the running game.
